verdict: Wrike: Choose Wrike when agency/enterprise work management with proofing, intake and reporting depth matters. Scores use the project-management editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing.
tradeoffs: Seat minimums and AI credit bundles vs published per-seat floors
Work OS breadth vs specialist timeline / PDF / remote / desktop depth
Automation and reporting depth vs ease of use for small teams
Included AI credits vs paid AI add-ons or credit top-ups
recommendation: Choose Wrike when agency/enterprise work management with proofing, intake and reporting depth matters. Compare Asana/monday for easier cross-functional defaults, ClickUp for value breadth, and Smartsheet for spreadsheet-native PMOs.
editorialNotes: Project-management Priority-2 batch. Approved on project-management-editorial v1.0.0. membershipRole=primary. jobCluster=work-os. handsOnTesting=false. Affiliate economics excluded.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Capable but denser than Asana — mid-market/agency admins cope well; SMB may feel heavier.
Strong project/folder structures, Gantt and resource-oriented planning.
Custom workflows and intake forms are a Wrike strength on Business+.
Proofing and cross-team collaboration fit creative/agency work.
Reporting and Work Intelligence analytics are a differentiator — 9.
Team $10 is fine; Business $25 is a steeper jump vs ClickUp/Asana. Affiliate economics excluded.
Work Intelligence AI present; not as consumer-visible as Notion/Motion AI.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the nine project-management editorial criteria using the category weights (work planning 15, automation & workflows 14, ease of use 12, collaboration 12, integrations 12, reporting 10, value 10, scalability 9, AI 6), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — work OS / PM peers, timeline specialists, and adjacent PDF / remote-access / desktop-workspace tools are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score, and affiliate economics are excluded.
